newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Lott considers smaller disaster aid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Lott considers smaller disaster aid.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott on Tuesday suggested splitting a bill for disaster relief and U.S. military operations abroad into two parts.
The first bill for $3.9 billion would be free of provisions that President Clinton has objected to.

This second bill for approximately $4.5 billion would include provisions sought by Republicans to prevent a government shutdown this fall and contain language to address their objections to the use of sampling surveys in the 2000 census, he said.
Lott ordered the Senate adjourned until 6 p.m. EDT (2200 GMT) after Democrats blocked the Senate from work on legislation and from holding committee meetings.
